run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Kubernetes evidence from namespace app-94 shows the app blue-whale is running (Deployment blue-whale 1/1 ready; pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r Running/Ready, restartCount 0) and is configured to reach its database at DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20. The database side is the observed problem: Service postgres in app-94 selects app=postgres-db, but its Endpoints object has no subsets, and no pod anywhere in the cluster carries the app=postgres-db label — the only pod in app-94 is blue-whale itself, the only ReplicaSet in app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (owned by Deployment blue-whale), and the only cluster-wide Service with port 5432 or a postgres name is app-94/postgres. So connection attempts from blue-whale to the postgres ClusterIP 10.96.191.39:5432 have no backend, which is the supported explanation for database connection timeouts (hypothesis, not a directly observed error). Namespace app-94, its Deployment and its pod were all created at 2026-11-21T07:11:19-07:11:20Z, i.e. seconds before this query, and the only events in the whole 24 h window are the six Normal blue-whale startup events, so no pre-existing incident history is visible. The pod is not failing in a Kubernetes sense: no restarts, no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff signals, and its own Service endpoint is populated. Direct proof of the app-level timeout — its own error logs, error spans or error-rate metrics — could not be obtained: the container has written nothing to stdout, the app code lives in an unreadable Secret, and both Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for this Run. No fault-injection setting was found; the namespace holds only the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap.

claims.text: Deployment blue-whale in app-94 (created 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z, replicas=1, ready=1, available=1) runs container blue-whale with image python:3.9-slim and command ['python','/app/app.py'], and its env sets DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20.

Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r in app-94 is phase Running, all conditions True including Ready, container blue-whale ready=true with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, startedAt 2026-11-21T07:11:20Z, owned by ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5.
Service postgres in app-94 is ClusterIP 10.96.191.39 with port 5432 -> targetPort 5432 and selector app=postgres-db.
In app-94 the Endpoints object postgres has subsets null (no addresses), while the Endpoints object blue-whale has address 10.244.0.104 pointing at pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r.

A cluster-wide pod listing returned 33 pods; the only pod in app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r with labels app=blue-whale,pod-template-hash=6bdbd444c5, and no returned pod carries the label app=postgres-db that Service postgres selects.

A cluster-wide Service query for port 5432 or a postgres-matching name returned exactly one Service: postgres in namespace app-94 (ClusterIP, ports 5432/5432, selector app=postgres-db); no other namespace provides a database Service on 5432.
The only ReplicaSet in app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (replicas=1, image python:3.9-slim, labels app=blue-whale), owned by Deployment blue-whale; there is no database ReplicaSet in the namespace.
The cluster-wide StatefulSet listing contains exactly one object, alertmanager in namespace otel-demo; there is no postgres StatefulSet in the cluster.

The only events inside the authorized window are six Normal events in app-94 timestamped 2026-11-21T07:11:19-07:11:20Z: Deployment blue-whale ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1', ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started.
Namespace app-94 was created at 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z, the same second as Deployment blue-whale and the startup events, so the workload and its namespace are younger than the 24 h authorized window.

The only ConfigMap in app-94 is kube-root-ca.crt (key ca.crt, created 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z); a cluster-wide ConfigMap query for names matching blue|postgres|db|pg or in app-94 returned no application or database ConfigMap, i.e. no fault-injection setting was observed there.
The blue-whale container mounts its application code from a Secret volume (name redacted in the projection) at /app, so the app.py code and its DB-connection behaviour could not be inspected.

Most likely cause of the reported database connection timeouts: blue-whale's DB target postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 resolves to ClusterIP Service postgres, which has no endpoints because no pod labelled app=postgres-db exists anywhere, so each connection attempt to the database has no backend and ends in a connect timeout rather than reaching a database. This matches 'No Database Endpoints: Database service has no backing pods' in the approved database-troubleshooting runbook, but the app-level timeout itself was not directly observed.

The missing database backend is a deployment gap in the new namespace rather than a runtime failure: app-94 (created 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z) contains only the blue-whale workload, and the returned listings show no postgres pod, ReplicaSet or StatefulSet in the cluster; i.e. the postgres workload that Service postgres expects was never created (or was never created with the app=postgres-db label), instead of having crashed.

Remaining candidate not resolved by this Run: connection-pool exhaustion or an application-side connect timeout inside blue-whale (DB_POOL_SIZE=20, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30) could also produce connection timeouts; it cannot be evaluated because the app writes no log lines and its code is in an unreadable Secret, and because no database exists to accept any connection in the first place.

Pod-level failure is not what the evidence shows for blue-whale: the pod is Running with all conditions True, the blue-whale container has restartCount 0, empty lastState and no previous container instance, and the only events in the window are Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started events — no Unhealthy, BackOff, OOMKilled or Evicted signal.

The blue-whale service routing itself is healthy: Service blue-whale has a populated Endpoints subset with address 10.244.0.104 referring to pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r and port 8080, so the app's own Service discovery is not the broken hop.

Rejected as the cause of the timeouts: blue-whale pod crash, OOM or eviction. The container has restartCount 0 with empty lastState, the pod is Ready, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff event or termination reason appears in the window's events for app-94.

Restore the database side in app-94: deploy (or re-create) a postgres workload labelled app=postgres-db so Service postgres gains endpoints, or, if the intended database pod carries another label, correct Service postgres' selector; then confirm Endpoints postgres has addresses before re-testing blue-whale's connections to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432.

To verify the app-side symptom on a future run, make the blue-whale container's stdout observable and its /app Secret accessible to the investigation, and restore Prometheus/Jaeger access so blue-whale's own error spans and error-rate metrics can be read rather than inferred.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every attempted call in this Run (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, list_prometheus_rules, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target all returned status=error, reason=SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so blue-whale error-rate, latency, connection-error and Kubernetes kube-state-metrics series could not be inspected; missing series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services returned status=error, reason=SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no blue-whale spans, error spans or parent-child call edges were observed and a complete call chain cannot be claimed.

No connection-error log line was observed: fetch_pod_logs for pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-sfl6r (default window and explicit 07:11:15-07:11:55Z) returned 0 lines with the current container stream status 'read' and no previous container instance, so whether the app logged a timeout is unknown.

The blue-whale application code is mounted from a Secret volume whose name is redacted, and Secrets cannot be read; the app's actual DB connect/retry logic and the effect of DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30 and DB_POOL_SIZE=20 could not be verified.

Whether a postgres Deployment ever existed cannot be stated as fact: the cluster-wide Deployment query filtered on names matching postgres|db|sql returned no rows with view status no_data (25 deployments processed), and deployments are only current state.
The cluster-wide NetworkPolicy query returned no objects and the view is not citable_as_fact, so NetworkPolicy blocking of app-94 -> postgres traffic is neither confirmed nor excluded.
ResourceQuota query returned no rows with view status no_data, so quota-driven absence of a database pod is not established either way.

Event history is thin: the only events inside the 24 h window are six Normal events at 2026-11-21T07:11:19-07:11:20Z (events expire and older ones were dropped), and namespace app-94 itself was created at 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z, so cluster activity before that instant is unknown.

No fault-injection switch was found on any object that was read (only ConfigMap in app-94 is kube-root-ca.crt), but other ConfigMaps in other namespaces were only examined by name pattern (blue|postgres|db|pg), so a fault setting held under an unrelated name was not ruled out.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so no record of what changed in app-94 before 2026-11-21T07:11:19Z is available.
Whether blue-whale itself is failing is unverified: no log line, error span or error-rate reading for that Deployment/Pod was observed, so it is not placed in the affected group.
next_steps: A platform operator should confirm whether a postgres workload is supposed to run in app-94 and, if so, why it is absent (deployment never applied versus removed), then restore it with label app=postgres-db or fix the Service selector accordingly.

Once a database pod is running, check 'kubectl get endpoints postgres -n app-94' shows the pod address and re-test connectivity from the blue-whale pod to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 (the runbook's nc/psql steps could not be executed here because no pod-exec tool is available in this Run).
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and re-check blue-whale error-rate/error spans and the blue-whale container's stdout for the exact timeout message before confirming the fault as resolved.
Review the Secret that supplies /app/app.py to confirm the connection timeout and pool settings actually used by the application.
